parts.part: Cards of mixed content, one playing a video with its controls

leaves.what: src/feed/VideoPlayer.tsx: a plain <video> element with a control bar under it, driven by the element's own events (play, pause, ended, timeupdate, durationchange, volumechange). The bar is the kit's: IconButton for play/pause, Slider for seeking, a toggle IconButton for mute, Body for the time. It pauses when it leaves the screen (IntersectionObserver).
leaves.why: The kit has no video or media player, and nothing that binds a media element to its controls.

leaves.what: Did not use CardContent; composed each card's insides as children (Title component="h2", Body, Label, a foot row).
leaves.why: CardContent draws its headline as headline-medium in a div: too large for a phone feed card, and not a heading a screen reader can list. It has no slot for a subhead/overline or for a foot with text and an action on one row (its doc says to compose those).

leaves.what: classNames={{ content: "p-0" }} on every Card so the media and the video run to the card's edges.
leaves.why: Card's doc: "To lay them out another way or to run them to the card's edges, say so on that part: `classNames={{ content: \"p-0\" }}`".

leaves.what: className="gap-0" on the Slider used as the seek bar.
leaves.why: With no label and showOutput={false} the Slider's grid still keeps the label row and its 8dp gap, so the track sits 8dp low beside the buttons. There is no bare/inline form.

leaves.what: formatOptions (unit: second) passed through to the Slider so the handle's value is read as "5 seconds".
leaves.why: The Slider has no value-label formatter (a function of the value), so the handle cannot say "0:05 of 0:20"; the clock time is written beside it as text instead.

leaves.what: The four card kinds (recipe, video, tip, collection), their text columns, the foot row, the collection's inner list, the tip's tertiary-container band.
leaves.why: A card's insides are the screen's.

leaves.what: A recipe's picture is a lucide icon on a tonal container (primary/secondary/tertiary-container), marked decorative. The video is a 20 s test pattern with a tone, generated locally with ffmpeg into public/media/, with a poster frame.
leaves.why: No web, so no photographs or real footage; nothing is hot-linked.

leaves.what: Card.tsx past its doc comment (how it detects media and drops the padding); Slider.tsx's body (its grid, what the thumb is named by, which props pass through).
leaves.why: The Slider's doc does not say how it lays out without label and output, nor that React Aria's formatOptions pass through.

parts.notes: Never run in a browser: verified by tsc, the build, the linter and one server render. Unexercised: playback, seeking by pointer and by arrow keys on the slider, mute, the pause on scroll-away. The video has no captions (it is a test pattern with a tone). No fullscreen control: in fullscreen the custom bar would be left behind. The Save toggle on each card works on state and shows a snackbar with Undo. The seek slider steps by one second. Card titles take useId() ids, since a saved item is drawn both in the hidden feed and in Saved.

leaves.what: Accepted the chips wrapping onto two rows at a phone's width; did not build the single scrolling row a phone feed usually has, and did not make the chips sticky (two rows pinned would take too much of a phone).
leaves.why: ChipGroup's className lands on its outer div; the row itself is hard-coded `flex flex-wrap gap-2` with no part to reach (no classNames, no data-slot on the inner group).

leaves.what: Chip.tsx's ChipGroup body.
leaves.why: To learn where className lands and that aria-label reaches the ToggleButtonGroup when there is no visible label (the doc speaks only of `label`).

leaves.what: A wrapper div with a ref around ChipGroup, and a querySelector for the first `[data-slot="chip"]`, to move the focus there after "Clear filters" removes itself.
leaves.why: ChipGroup takes no ref and has no way to be focused from outside.

parts.notes: Multiple selection, AND between chips; they drive the list's filter text and the mock server filters. Vegan + Dessert (or Video + Dessert) matches nothing and reaches the empty state. Not exercised in a browser.

leaves.what: useAsyncList from react-aria-components holds the pages, the cursor (an item's id), the filter text and the abort of a stale request; its items go to a plain <ul>, not a GridList.
leaves.why: The skill's table names it for "a list that is ... loaded as it is scrolled", but only with GridList/Table. A feed of cards holding a slider and buttons cannot be grid rows (the grid takes the arrow keys).

leaves.what: An IntersectionObserver on a sentinel after the list calls loadMore(); it is made again after each load so a short page in a tall window asks for the next. The feed ends with a line saying so, and a visually hidden status says how many are shown.
leaves.why: The kit has nothing that says "the end came into view" outside a collection component. Nobody operates it, so it is logged as layout.

leaves.what: Wrote list.cursor to know whether more follows; AsyncListData does not expose it. Also took the list's first state for `loading`: it is `idle` until its effect runs, so the empty state showed on the first paint (caught by a server render, not by the build). Fixed with two flags of the project's own, hasMore and hasLoaded, set in load().
leaves.why: Neither is in the skill or in the hook's types' comments; a line in the skill on "is there more" and on the first render would have saved both.

parts.notes: 22 mock items, 6 a page, 1.1 s a page. Not exercised in a browser: the observer, the abort on a filter change, StrictMode's double effect (reasoned, not seen).

leaves.what: Edited the block: a `fab` prop, drawn absolute at the content's bottom trailing corner while the window is compact, before `main` in the document so Tab reaches it without crossing the feed; from 600dp the same FAB is the rail's `railHeader`.
leaves.why: The block's comment: "Yours to change: a drawer in place of the expanded rail, a FAB in the rail's `header`, an account button in its `footer`, other widths." It has a place for a FAB on the rail and none over the content on a phone.

leaves.what: SnackbarRegion className="bottom-40 sm:bottom-4" so a snackbar clears the bar and the FAB.
leaves.why: Snackbar's doc: "Place the region with `className` when the layout has a bottom navigation bar or a FAB the snackbar must sit above (`bottom-20 sm:bottom-4`)".

leaves.what: The dialog's form (name field, tag chips, Cancel and Add) as children of ModalDialog, with its own Headline.
leaves.why: ModalDialog's structured form has no place for fields.

parts.notes: The FAB opens a dialog that adds a recipe to the mock server and to the top of the feed; if the filters hide it the snackbar offers to clear them. The block switches at 600px of its own width, the snackbar at Tailwind's sm (640px of the window): between the two a snackbar sits higher than it needs to. Not exercised in a browser.

leaves.what: Edited the block: the compact bar is moved before the content in the document and drawn last with `order-last`.
leaves.why: The block's comment: "it is copied into your project to be edited. It is yours from then on". As shipped the bar comes after `main`, so under an endless feed Tab reaches it only when the feed ends.

leaves.what: The views behind the destinations: Home (the feed, kept mounted and hidden so its pages survive), Saved (the saved cards, or an EmptyState), and one line each for Explore and Profile.
leaves.why: Explore and Profile are other screens; they are stated as not built rather than faked.

parts.notes: `npx shadcn@latest add @ds/app-shell-block -y` was refused by this session's permission layer, so kit-blocks/AppShell.tsx was copied to src/components/AppShell.tsx, as the brief allows. Destinations are buttons on state, not routes: no address and no Back. The Saved destination carries a badge with the count. From 600dp the block shows the rail instead (expanded from 1200dp). Not exercised in a browser. Coming back to Home keeps the loaded pages but not the scroll position.

leaves.what: Six card-shaped placeholders in a SkeletonGroup given the feed's grid; text skeletons inside the type primitives they replace, sizes by className.
leaves.why: Skeleton's doc: "Size it with `className`", "Put it inside the type primitive it replaces", and SkeletonGroup's "give it the layout of the content it stands for".

leaves.what: `rounded-none` on the rectangle that stands for the card's edge-to-edge picture.
leaves.why: A rectangle always takes the medium corner; inside a card that already clips there is no square form.

leaves.what: FeedCardSkeleton, the shape of a recipe card.
leaves.why: The placeholder's shape is the screen's.

parts.notes: Shown on the first load and after every filter change (the server render shows 36 skeleton elements on first paint). Loading a further page shows a LoadingIndicator under the list instead.

Reached with filters that match nothing (Vegan + Dessert); its action clears the filters. A second one stands in Saved when nothing is saved, and a third would show if a load failed (the mock never fails). size="sm" with a lucide icon as media. Not exercised in a browser. Its button is removed by its own press, so the focus is moved to the first filter chip. Un-saving a card in Saved moves the focus to the shell's main (id app-shell-main, the block's own). Neither focus move was exercised.

general_leaves.what: The page: `h-dvh` root, the feed's column with a container query (one, two, three columns of cards by the content's own width), 96px of bottom padding so the FAB covers no card's action.
general_leaves.why: A page's layout is the screen's.

general_leaves.what: Past the doc comments, for facts used: Button.tsx and IconButton.tsx (the prop types: icon, isToggle, onChange, the fab size), EmptyState.tsx (the media's type), DialogContent.tsx and ModalDialog.tsx (children in place of the structured parts, isOpen/onClose), Skeleton.tsx, TopAppBar.tsx's props, Badge.tsx (a count of 0 gives no badge and no words), Typography.tsx (the colorRole list, that `component` takes h2), BottomNavigation.tsx's item type, Snackbar.tsx's region classes.
general_leaves.why: Most are prop types that sit just under the doc comment; a props table in each doc comment would end the reading.

general_leaves.what: Verification without a browser: a one-off server render of App (tsx, renderToString) to count skeletons on first paint. The first attempt wrote its script one directory above the project (rerun-091/ssr-08.tsx), outside the brief's boundary; it was removed at once and the check redone from a file inside the project, also removed.
general_leaves.why: The brief forbids a browser and a dev server; the build alone could not show the first-paint empty state.

friction: 1. Nothing in the kit or the skill covers media: a video card is a likely feed part, and the pieces exist (IconButton, Slider), but the Slider has no bare inline form (label row and gap stay) and no value formatter, so a seek bar is two reaches. 2. ChipGroup cannot be a single scrolling row: its className is the outer div's and the row is hard-coded to wrap; a `classNames.list` or a `wrap={false}` would do it. 3. useAsyncList is named in the skill only beside GridList/Table; for a list of cards with controls inside, the skill could say: plain ul, IntersectionObserver sentinel, that AsyncListData hides its cursor (keep your own hasMore) and that it is `idle`, not `loading`, on the first render. That last one passes the build and shows an empty state for a frame. 4. AppShell has a FAB place on the rail but none on a phone, and its bar comes after main in the document: under a long or endless page a keyboard user cannot reach it. Both were short edits, but every feed will make them. 5. CardContent's headline is headline-medium in a div; a feed wants a smaller, real heading, so CardContent goes unused and the card's padding rule (dropped only when CardContent with media is a direct child) has to be learned from the source. 6. The shadcn add command was refused by the session's permissions; the kit-blocks/ copy made that painless.
